name: Fastcapades
about: Fasting in practice and theory: religious observance, metabolic health, protocols, physiology debates, refeeding, and the interior and social life of voluntary abstention.

topics.name: Primary purpose
topics.question: What is the highest, most legitimate purpose of voluntary abstention from food?

hovertip.issue: What is the highest, most legitimate purpose of voluntary abstention from food?

poles.label: Metabolic & Longevity Repair
poles.text: Periodic fasting triggers cellular cleanup, insulin sensitivity, and metabolic flexibility that constant grazing prevents.

poles.label: Sacred Devotion & Obedience
poles.text: Fasting humbles bodily appetite before God and aligns the believer with sacred command and penitence.

poles.label: Mental Clarity & Detachment
poles.text: Stepping off the feeding treadmill sharpens focus and proves the mind is not a slave to every impulse.

poles.label: Moral Protest & Solidarity
poles.text: Refusing nourishment in solidarity with the hungry or against injustice turns the body itself into a witness.

hovertip.issue: Should fasting be approached as a transformative moral and spiritual practice, or as a neutral physiological tool like sleep or exercise?

poles.label: Contemplative Soul-Shaping
poles.text: Stripping fasting of prayer, gratitude, and self-examination reduces a sacred discipline to mechanical biohacking.

poles.label: Secular Biological Maintenance
poles.text: Grounding fasting in measurable metabolic physiology keeps it practical, testable, and accessible regardless of creed.

hovertip.issue: Is fasting something owed, or something chosen?

poles.label: Commanded Observance
poles.text: The fast is commanded by God or tradition; obedience is the point.

poles.label: Chosen Discipline
poles.text: No one commands it; its value lies precisely in being freely taken up.

hovertip.issue: Is using fasting primarily to lose body fat a smart, simple strategy, or does it distort the practice into chronic dieting?

poles.label: Pragmatic Fat-Loss Lever
poles.text: Clear eating windows eliminate snacking without tedious calorie counting and tap stored body fat directly.

poles.label: Keep Weight Goals Separate
poles.text: Treating fasts as weight-loss punishment breeds binge-restrict cycles and obscures deeper metabolic and contemplative benefits.

hovertip.issue: How strong is the scientific case for fasting?

poles.label: Clinically Proven
poles.text: Controlled trials already justify fasting as therapy for metabolic disease.

poles.label: Promising & Mixed
poles.text: Animal data is strong and human data is coming, but the headlines run ahead of both.

poles.label: Mostly Tradition
poles.text: The practice is ancient and meaningful; the laboratory case remains thin.

hovertip.issue: Does a true fast demand pure water alone, or may black coffee, tea, and tiny caloric buffers be included without losing the point?

poles.label: Strict Zero-Calorie Water Only
poles.text: Anything beyond plain water — even bitter compounds or sweeteners — triggers digestive signaling and dilutes clean physiological rest.

poles.label: Clean Non-Caloric Aids
poles.text: Black coffee, plain tea, and unflavored electrolytes preserve insulin and autophagy benefits while making fasts sustainable in daily life.

poles.label: Pragmatic Dirty Fasting
poles.text: A splash of cream or bone broth under fifty calories keeps adherence high while delivering nearly identical metabolic results.

hovertip.issue: Is abstaining from water alongside food a valid religious and metabolic practice, or an unnecessary physiological hazard?

poles.label: Always Hydrate Generously
poles.text: Water supports kidney clearance, circulation, and safe ketone adaptation without risking dehydration injury.

poles.label: Dawn-to-Dusk or Short Dry Fasts
poles.text: Sacred traditions like Ramadan and Yom Kippur sanctify complete abstention, and brief dry windows accelerate metabolic water production.

hovertip.issue: Should extended fasters proactively supplement electrolytes, or trust the body’s renal conservation mechanisms?

poles.label: Active Sodium, Potassium & Magnesium
poles.text: Natriuresis of fasting flushes minerals rapidly; supplementing prevents headaches, cramps, and orthostatic dizziness.

poles.label: Pure Unsupplemented Water
poles.text: Healthy kidneys conserve electrolytes naturally during multi-day fasts, whereas salty drinks irritate an empty stomach.

hovertip.issue: Can structured low-calorie or restricted-food protocols capture the benefits of fasting, or only complete abstention?

poles.label: True Zero-Intake Abstention
poles.text: Only complete cessation of digestion flips the full metabolic switch into deep ketosis and gut rest.

poles.label: Fasting-Mimicking & Daniel Fasts
poles.text: Targeted low-protein, low-calorie rations trigger cellular stress pathways safely while nourishing people who cannot do water fasts.

topics.name: Cadence & duration
topics.question: Which fasting rhythm fits human physiology and real life best?

hovertip.issue: Which fasting rhythm fits human physiology and real life best?

poles.label: Daily Time-Restricted (16:8–20:4)
poles.text: Aligning eating with daylight circadian rhythms is gentle, sustainable for years, and socially effortless.

poles.label: One Meal a Day (OMAD)
poles.text: Compressing nourishment into one daily feast simplifies life and trains steady appetite control.

poles.label: Alternate-Day / 36–48h
poles.text: Full-day fasts separated by normal eating days deliver deep insulin drops without multi-day refeeding complexity.

poles.label: Multi-Day Extended (3–7+ Days)
poles.text: Crossing the seventy-two-hour mark unlocks profound ketosis, mental stillness, and immune reset impossible in short windows.

poles.label: Liturgical Seasonal Calendars
poles.text: Synchronizing fasts with communal feasts and sacred seasons roots bodily discipline in shared heritage rather than solitary willpower.

hovertip.issue: When practicing daily time-restricted eating, is it better to skip dinner or skip breakfast?

poles.label: Early Daylight Eating Window
poles.text: Insulin sensitivity and digestive thermogenesis peak in the morning, making late-night calories metabolically costly.

poles.label: Evening Dinner Window
poles.text: Sharing dinner with family and friends preserves social life and matches natural daytime alertness while working.

hovertip.issue: Does fasting work best with strict non-negotiable rules, or by skipping meals organically when true hunger is absent?

poles.label: Fixed Clock & Calendar Rules
poles.text: Clear pre-commitments eliminate constant negotiation with cravings and build dependable habit momentum.

poles.label: Flexible Appetite-Led Windows
poles.text: Listening to real energy, stress, and social rhythms prevents rigid rule-following from overriding bodily wisdom.

hovertip.issue: When does clinically meaningful autophagy actually ramp up in human tissues during a fast?

poles.label: Active Within 16–24 Hours
poles.text: Liver glycogen depletion and rising glucagon begin upregulating cellular recycling within a single day of fasting.

poles.label: Requires 48–72+ Hours
poles.text: Mouse timelines compress human metabolism; deep tissue autophagy in humans takes multiple days without protein or insulin spikes.

poles.label: Unmeasurable Outside Lab Biopsies
poles.text: We currently lack reliable blood biomarkers for human autophagy, so confident hourly claims outrun the science.

hovertip.issue: Does extended fasting protect skeletal muscle through ketones and growth hormone, or inevitably catabolize precious lean tissue?

poles.label: Growth Hormone & Ketones Spare Muscle
poles.text: Rising ketones and pulsatile growth hormone dramatically reduce protein oxidation once fat adaptation kicks in.

poles.label: Prolonged Fasts Erode Lean Mass
poles.text: Without dietary amino acids or mechanical stimulus, multi-day fasts sacrifice hard-won muscle alongside fat.

hovertip.issue: How should physical exercise be paired with a fasting window?

poles.label: Train Hard Fasted
poles.text: Lifting or running fasted amplifies catecholamines, fat oxidation, and mitochondrial adaptation without heavy digestion.

poles.label: Gentle Zone-2 & Mobility Only
poles.text: Light walking and stretching stimulate circulation and muscle retention without spiking cortisol or hypoglycemia.

poles.label: Rest & Conserve Energy
poles.text: Heavy training during extended fasts compounds recovery stress; fasting days belong to stillness and repair.

hovertip.issue: Is the wired, alert feeling during a fast a sign of clean evolutionary sharpness, or a sympathetic stress response?

poles.label: Energizing Noradrenaline Focus
poles.text: Mild orexin and noradrenaline elevation during fasting sharpens alertness so an organism can forage effectively.

poles.label: Hidden HPA-Axis Stress Cost
poles.text: Frequent prolonged fasts elevate cortisol and fragment deep sleep, quietly taxing thyroid and recovery.

hovertip.issue: Should women of reproductive age modify or pause fasting around hormonal phases, or do core metabolic rules apply equally?

poles.label: Cycle-Synced & Cautious Protocols
poles.text: Female reproductive hormones are acutely sensitive to energy deficits, especially in the late luteal phase before menstruation.

poles.label: Uniform Human Physiology
poles.text: Ancestral humans of both sexes endured unpredictable food gaps; moderate fasting supports metabolic health across sexes without over-medicalizing.

hovertip.issue: How should a fast end?

poles.label: Small & Gentle
poles.text: Broth, eggs, something small: wake the gut up slowly.

poles.label: A Normal Meal
poles.text: Eat a normal meal and get on with life; ceremony is superstition.

poles.label: The Planned Feast
poles.text: The feast is part of the fast; plan it, cook it, honor it.

hovertip.issue: How dangerous is eating again after a fast?

poles.label: Casual at Any Length
poles.text: Healthy people refeed fine; refeeding syndrome belongs to starvation, not fasting.

poles.label: Careful Past 48 Hours
poles.text: After two days, stage the return: small, low-carb, electrolytes first.

poles.label: Medical Past 5 Days
poles.text: Past five days, refeeding is a medical procedure and should be treated as one.

poles.label: A Broken Fast Is a Failed Fast

hovertip.issue: You ate at hour 30 of 48. What just happened?

poles.label: Data, Not Failure
poles.text: The fast taught you where your edge is; log it and go again.

poles.label: A Broken Fast Is a Failed Fast
poles.text: The commitment was the practice; eating early means the fast did not happen.

hovertip.issue: Should you keep your fasting private so it never inconveniences or lectures others, or talk about it openly?

poles.label: Keep Fasts Quiet & Unannounced
poles.text: Anointing your head and hiding your fast prevents spiritual vanity and spares hosts awkwardness at dinner.

poles.label: Openly Share & Normalize Practice
poles.text: Explaining why you are skipping lunch removes stigma, builds community support, and helps curious friends learn.

hovertip.issue: When a loved one cooks or a celebration gathers around food, which duty wins: hospitality or your fasting commitment?

poles.label: Break Fast for Sacred Hospitality
poles.text: Monastic wisdom holds that love and fellowship outrank personal austerity; you can always fast tomorrow.

poles.label: Hold Line With Graceful Presence
poles.text: Sitting warmly at the table with tea or water shows that human company does not require eating.

hovertip.issue: Should the fasting cook keep cooking for the household?

poles.label: An Act of Service
poles.text: Preparing food you will not eat, for people you love, is the fast made visible as service.

poles.label: A Needless Temptation
poles.text: Standing over tasting spoons all day is fighting the fast on hard mode for no benefit.

hovertip.issue: When hunger pangs arrive during a planned fast, should you sit with them calmly or treat them as a stop sign?

poles.label: Passing Wave to Observe
poles.text: Ghrelin rises at habitual mealtimes and subsides within an hour; watching hunger pass builds quiet inner freedom.

poles.label: Biological Alarm to Honor
poles.text: Persistent dizziness, coldness, or gnawing distress is honest somatic feedback telling you to nourish the body.

hovertip.issue: What does hunger actually feel like across a fast?

poles.label: White-Knuckle Endurance
poles.text: It is endurance: a wall to lean on until the clock releases you.

poles.label: Waves That Pass
poles.text: Hunger comes in waves tied to habit and ghrelin, and each wave passes in twenty minutes.

poles.label: The Clarity Window
poles.text: Past the waves there is a lucid, quiet window that is the real prize.

hovertip.issue: How firmly should communities warn away people with past eating disorders, pregnancy, or fragility from fasting?

poles.label: Strict Exclusion Gatekeeping
poles.text: Fasting can rapidly reactivate restrictive disorders or harm pregnancy and growth, demanding clear bright-line warnings.

poles.label: Autonomous Adult Self-Experimentation
poles.text: Informed adults can judge their own medical context with their doctors without paternalistic bans.

hovertip.issue: Is fasting a solitary discipline or a communal one?

poles.label: Solitary Retreat
poles.text: Going apart — monastery, cabin, desert — is how the fast has always deepened.

poles.label: Communal & Calendar-Bound
poles.text: Ramadan and Lent are fasted together, on a calendar, or they lose their power.

prompt.opening: Write an informed discussion between the stances recorded on this map.
rules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Show where the stances agree, where they part, and what follows from each position.
Use the recorded ratings as emphasis: 80–100 central, 56–79 strong support, 36–55 lighter, and 0–35 optional curiosity.
Use only the named topics below. Do not add, imply, or reference any unlisted stance.
Do not invent positions, sources, or facts beyond the supplied data.
prompt.rigor: At maximum depth, length, and rigor, write at dissertation-defense standard: state each position precisely, raise the strongest objections to each, answer them, and defend the conclusion against a skeptical examiner.

phases.help: Enabled phases are added to the generated prompt as a Discussion structure section, in opening, development, closing order. Turn a phase off to leave it out.

groundRules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Speak from your own recorded stance; don't speak for the other side.
Take turns: one position at a time, each side heard fully before replies.
Objections go to the position, not the person holding it.
Anyone may call a pause; the discussion resumes only when everyone is ready.
What the profiles agree on is common ground — start there, and return to it when the discussion stalls.
